items.problem: Bootstrap omitted project-linked source files outside the supplied Source directory.
items.evidence: PersonalDataEncryption.csproj declares linked App.xaml, MainPage, scenario XAML, styles, code, and assets; session-log.txt turns 8-16 show missing source globs followed by generated-obj XAML reconstruction.
items.skill_search: Searched Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 and SKILL.md for Link, linked, SharedContent, Page Include, and Compile Include.
items.root_cause: Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 used only a recursive directory walk under Source and never evaluated declared project items or their Link destinations.
items.proposed_fix: Extend bootstrap to resolve common UWP project properties and copy declared external Compile/Page/ApplicationDefinition/Content/Resource items to their Link paths.
items.generalizes: Legacy UWP solutions and Microsoft SDK samples routinely share shell XAML, styles, code, and assets through linked csproj items.

items.problem: The skill instructed agents to compile with nonexistent `winapp build`.
items.evidence: session-log.txt turn 25: winapp returned "'build' was not matched" and listed no build subcommand.
items.skill_search: Searched the migration skill for `winapp build`; found it in SKILL.md Step 3/final validation and Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 comments.
items.root_cause: The guidance conflated winapp's run/package surface with .NET compilation.
items.proposed_fix: Replace compile instructions with `dotnet build <project.csproj>` and state that winapp has no build subcommand.
items.generalizes: Every C# WinUI migration needs a reliable compile command before launch and validation.

items.problem: The skill did not classify UserDataProtectionManager as unavailable for preserving UWP lock-state protection semantics in WinUI desktop.
items.evidence: migration-score.json reports both features failed because only the unavailable fallback rendered; migrated Scenario1_Files.xaml.cs and Scenario2_Memory.xaml.cs hide AvailablePanel when TryGetDefault returns null.
items.skill_search: Searched SKILL.md, MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, scripts, and unsupported-api-inventory.json for UserDataProtectionManager, UserDataAvailability, and DataProtection; no migration guidance or inventory entry existed.
items.root_cause: The Windows projection compiles, but runtime availability differs in the full-trust desktop process and no desktop API preserves AfterFirstUnlock/WhileUnlocked semantics; build/process-alive checks therefore produced a false success.
items.proposed_fix: Add UserDataProtectionManager to the machine-readable unsupported inventory and explain the compile-versus-runtime trap and non-equivalent DPAPI fallback in MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md.
items.generalizes: Other UWP apps use personal-data protection APIs that compile in desktop projects but become permanently unavailable at runtime.
